integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] An original expressive 3D CG animated Brazilian street-news comedy at a peaceful protest by adult PC gamers. One uninterrupted static eye-level medium-long full-body portrait shot,768x1344,15seconds. Reporter screen-left, gamer screen-right, both fully original fictional adults, lively faces, visible hands and solid grounded bodies. A small asynchronous adult crowd stands behind them in a warm Brazilian square. Soft afternoon sunlight from screen-left, colorful matte clothes, coherent contact shadows. Plain red-brick storefront and plain navy awning. No existing character, real person, store name or numerical price claim. No violence, fire, weapons or damage.
Exactly TWO enormous plain pale ivory BLANK paper protest boards high above every head, fully front-facing, rectangular and nearly still. Left paper stays within x28to356, right within x412to740. Both boards lie above y480, with a generous air gap between the paper and all hair, hands, microphones and bodies. Both boards and all four corners stay fully visible for the entire shot. Separate supporters hold the wooden poles far below the papers. No occlusion and no board bouncing during laughter or chanting. Exactly two boards, no other signs. All paper surfaces have absolutely no letters, numbers, symbols, drawings or texture marks. Exact huge lettering will be composited later. Leave the upper navy awning plain without writing. All clothing, microphone and computer props are unbranded. No subtitles or other on-screen text.

Static eye-level medium-long full-body portrait interview, head to hiking-boot soles. Keep both adults heads below y490 and their feet inside y1280. Ground plane and contact shadows are visible, no cut-off boots. Huge blank boards above the hair occupy the upper third. Same warm brick storefront and plain navy awning, different interview pair and no continuing action across the editorial boundary.

A different interview pair. Reporter: original adult woman with warm brown skin, long dark braid and burgundy jacket, screen-left. Gamer: original adult man with short brown hair, olive hiking shirt, dark knee-length hiking shorts, a plain backpack worn on both shoulders and chunky tan hiking boots, screen-right. All adults, no existing characters or real-person likenesses.

No table or computer props. His backpack stays worn and both boots stay firmly planted. He grasps one shoulder strap once in mock expedition readiness, then proudly squares his shoulders. Do not walk, run, stamp, transfer objects or touch the reporter. The comic visual is his travel outfit and confident answer.

He treats a ridiculous cross-country walk as a sensible money-saving plan. Deliver the first sentence with decisive practical confidence, then widen into mock heroic determination on atravesso o Brasil. The reporter looks down toward the hiking boots, back to his confident face, understands the absurdity and laughs only after his last word. His straight face then breaks and he joins the laugh. Background adults react later and asynchronously.

ACTING SCORE: Play the ridiculous answer as a sincere attempt to convince the reporter. Start with engaged curiosity and attentive listening, not constant grinning. One dominant meaningful gesture accompanies the answer. The reporter perceives the punchline only after its final word, glances briefly toward the relevant prop, then tries to suppress a smile and fails. The laugh is clearly visible and AUDIBLE: microphone lowers to waist, eyes squeeze, head tips back briefly, then a small forward lean with two uneven shoulder bounces and one hand against the abdomen. The gamer holds a straight face for a short recognition beat, then cracks into an amused grin and joins with a shorter irregular voiced laugh. Nearby supporters react later and differently; no synchronized mechanical swaying. Both catch their breath and exchange an amused look. Laughter must have a cause in this exchange. Keep feet planted, prop supported and boards motionless. No frozen faces, talking-mouth-only acting, anticipation before the joke, flat monotone or tiny polite chuckle.

Exactly THREE verbal turns in native Brazilian Portuguese. Reporter(S1), an adult female voice, asks once at 0.2 to 2.4 seconds, curious and attentive: <d>[Portuguese] E como você vai resolver?</d> Reporter then listens with closed lips. Gamer(S2), an adult male voice, answers once at 2.8 to 7.8 seconds, with clear ordinary conversational Brazilian Portuguese diction, mock seriousness and a brief pause between sentences: <d>[Portuguese] Vou buscar a pé! Pelo preço desse frete, eu atravesso o Brasil!</d> No repeated words or additional utterances. Reporter reacts only after the last word, with a short recognition beat, an unsuccessful attempt to hold a smile, microphone lowered below the mouth, then a clear AUDIBLE warm voiced belly laugh. Eyes close, shoulders bounce twice unevenly, body leans forward briefly and recovers. Gamer joins later with a shorter clearly audible spontaneous laugh. The crowd reacts after the two leads, with different timing, never synchronized swaying. Laughing is nonverbal: no invented words, babble or extra syllables. Let laughter resolve by 10.1 seconds. At 10.5 to 13.5 seconds the adult supporters chant ONCE: <d>[Portuguese] Mais FPS, menos frete!</d> The reporter and gamer are silent and smiling during the chant. Recover with an exchanged amused look from 13.5 to 15 seconds. No additional speech.

One static continuous shot, normal speed, no cuts or zoom. Only specified exact dialogue tags contain spoken words. Laughter is native in-scene nonverbal voiced laughter with irregular breaths, not extra syllables or words. No canned laugh track, narrator, music, subtitles, logos, watermarks or added verbal remarks. Keep background street ambience soft under dialogue and laughter.
overall_soundscape: Expressive clearly intelligible on-screen native Brazilian Portuguese voices and spontaneous warm voiced laughter synchronized with bodily reactions, with low outdoor ambience.
